pois.name: Akihabara Station
pois.description: The gateway to Electric Town — the station's 'Akihabara' exit opens onto a district where every building houses multiple floors of electronics, anime goods, and manga. The elevated track viaduct frames the street below with neon signs competing for attention.

pois.name: Animate Akihabara
pois.description: Japan's largest anime, manga, and game retailer — 8 floors of character goods, manga volumes, Blu-rays, and figures. The flagship store rotates themed floors by franchise season and draws thousands of fans daily.

pois.name: Yodobashi Camera Akiba
pois.description: Tokyo's largest electronics megastore — 9 floors of cameras, computers, appliances and games with tax-free shopping. The rooftop has a camera test course and the basement a gourmet food hall.

pois.name: Super Potato Retro Games
pois.description: Legendary retro game store spanning 3 floors — Famicom, Super Famicom, Mega Drive, and PlayStation classics in original boxes. The second floor is a playable museum with vintage consoles. A pilgrimage site for gaming historians worldwide.

pois.name: Kanda Myojin Shrine
pois.description: A grand Shinto shrine established in 730 AD, now the guardian deity of Akihabara and Tokyo's tech industry. IT companies come to have their servers blessed here. The colourful main gate and modern otaku ema (votive plaques) make it the spiritual heart of Electric Town.
